content.value_statement: Creating reliable AI agents requires clear triggers, tools, and system prompts. This skill provides templates, examples, and validation guidance for Claude Code plugin agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Claude Code agent file format and required frontmatter fields.
Shows how to write triggering descriptions with examples and commentary.
Provides system prompt structures with responsibilities, process steps, and output formats.
Includes complete examples for review, testing, documentation, and security agents.
Documents model, color, and tool access choices for plugin agents.
Includes a local shell validator for agent markdown structure.
limitations: It focuses on Claude Code plugin agents, not every multi-agent framework.
The validator uses shell text parsing and may not handle complex YAML perfectly.
Example agents need customization before production use.
It does not automatically test agent behavior inside Claude Code.

use_cases.title: Create a New Plugin Agent
use_cases.description: Use the templates to define frontmatter, triggers, tools, and a structured system prompt.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Triggering
use_cases.description: Refine descriptions with concrete examples so Claude Code selects the agent at the right time.

use_cases.title: Validate Agent Files
use_cases.description: Run the included checks to catch missing fields, weak descriptions, and prompt structure issues.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first agent file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Claude Code agent for [task]. Define the name, description, model, color, tools, and system prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Trigger Examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve when an existing agent should activate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent description and add clearer trigger examples with context, user request, assistant action, and commentary.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Specialized Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Build an agent for a focused engineering workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a specialized agent for [domain]. Include responsibilities, analysis process, quality standards, edge cases, and output format.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Suite
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of several plugin agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these agent files for trigger overlap, excessive tool access, weak prompts, missing validation, and inconsistent output expectations.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that reviews TypeScript code after implementation.
output_examples.output: A complete agent plan with a descriptive name, review-focused triggers, least-privilege tools, and a structured review process.

output_examples.input: My agent does not trigger when users ask for tests.
output_examples.output: A revised trigger description with concrete examples for explicit test requests and proactive test generation after code changes.

output_examples.input: Validate this agent file before I add it to a plugin.
output_examples.output: A checklist of required frontmatter, description quality, tool access, system prompt coverage, and validation script results.

best_practices: Use specific trigger examples that show context, user intent, and expected agent use.
Limit tools to the minimum required for the agent task.
Define responsibilities, process steps, edge cases, and output format in every system prompt.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague agent names or generic descriptions.
Do not grant all tools when read-only access is enough.
Do not omit testing for trigger behavior and output quality.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build Claude Code plugin agents with clear frontmatter, triggers, tool choices, and system prompts.

faq.question: Does it create agent files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides templates and guidance. You still create or edit the agent files in your plugin.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the guidance to draft, review, and improve Claude Code agent files.

faq.question: What tools should an agent receive?
faq.answer: Choose the smallest tool set that supports the task. Prefer read-only tools for analysis agents.

faq.question: How do I know an agent will trigger correctly?
faq.answer: Write concrete examples in the description, then test requests that match and differ from those examples.

faq.question: Is the included validator a full YAML parser?
faq.answer: No. It performs practical shell-based checks and may miss complex frontmatter edge cases.
